content:
alec: quick check — ran an overnight SKU sweep (H100 / A100 / L40S) against the same 8k longctx prompt set, batch=1. saw intermittent p99 spikes on H100 around 200-300ms above baseline. posting short logs and command I used.

fiona: thanks for the heads up. did you pin driver versions / MIG configs?

alec: no MIG. drivers: nvidia-driver 535.113, cuda 12.1. kernel 6.1. ran on fresh instance alloc, no other user traffic.

dan: can you paste the bench command + small output sample?

alec: sure — command:
```
./run_sweep.sh --skus h100,a100,l40s --model redwood-v2-1b --ctx 8192 --batch 1 --iters 1000 --collect-quantiles --tags=overnight-sweep
```
sample aggregated p50/p95/p99 (ms per-token):
H100: p50=3.2  p95=9.6  p99=24.1
A100: p50=3.9  p95=10.2 p99=11.8
L40S: p50=4.3  p95=12.0 p99=13.5

carol: whoa H100 p99 much higher than A100 — suggests a tail event. any microburst logs or nvlink errors?

alec: infra-bot captured GPU sched events, attaching excerpt:
```
[2026-03-15T02:14:21Z] SCHED_DELAY gpu0 0.0023
[2026-03-15T02:14:21Z] MIGRATE_WAIT gpu0->gpu1 0.0008
[2026-03-15T02:14:21Z] KERNEL_RETRY gpu0 0.0051
```

fiona: looks like a few kernel retries in the same window. are we falling back to different kernels (e.g., bf16->fp16) when seq len spikes?

alec: runtime logs show kernel selection changed for token positions > 4096, switching to small-block kernel on H100. config excerpt:
```
kernel_policy: dynamic
sequence_thresholds: [1024,4096]
fallback_kernel: small-block
```

dan: could be that the small-block kernel is sensitive to memory bandwidth contention on H100 config. can you repro with disabled fallback? set kernel_policy=static for H100 and rerun small sample (100 iters) and post p99 diff?

alec: starting a 100-iter job now with static kernel. will post results in ~10m.

infra-bot: job 7721 queued on h100-pool-09 (allocated: 1xH100). ETA ~2m.

(10m later)
alec: quick results — static kernel p99 dropped from 24.1 -> 12.5 ms (half). A100 unchanged. short log: H100 p99=12.5 ms, p95=9.3 ms.

carol: that strongly points to a kernel fallback path being the culprit. can you capture perf counters (L2_bw, l2_hit) on the next run? especially around the tokens where it switches.

alec: will enable perf and redo overnight short sweep.

fiona: also file a bench task with config and attach links to the profiling artifacts. add label: h100-tail, kernel-fallback. ping me for review before filing.

alec: will do. thanks. :thumbsup:

carol: nice triage. if it repros, we should consider smoothing the threshold or improving the small-block kernel. adding to hw-bench backlog once artifacts exist.

infra-bot: note: h100-pool-09 went under maintenance window 2026-03-15T04:00Z — check if any overlap with overnight sweep.

alec: good catch — my sweep window overlapped by ~3m with maintenance; rerunning on h100-pool-12 (no maintenance). will update when done.

dan: thanks — this is actionable. possible next steps: (1) gather perf counters + kernel traces, (2) repro with static kernel -> confirm, (3) long run to see stability, (4) follow up with kernel owner if small-block shows pathological behavior.

fiona: i'll help with filing and triage doc after you upload artifacts.

alec: uploading traces now and will create bench task in 30m.
